title: Bulk edit ergonomics: distribute tasks across Kanban buckets
description: Probes whether the agent discovers vikunja_task_bulk's bulk-set-bucket operation (src/tools/tasks/buckets.ts's bulkSetTaskBucket, one call moves a whole group of task ids into a single bucket) rather than moving each task into its column one at a time via vikunja_tasks set-bucket. RE-BASELINED 2026-07-25 (netadvanced/vikunja-mcp#28 C1): this scenario's own prompt (new project, N-column Kanban board, tasks distributed across those columns by name) is now a verbatim match for vikunja_projects' setup-kanban composite (PR #175, src/tools/projects/kanban-setup.ts) -- ONE call creates the project, the three named buckets in order, all 9 tasks (each carrying its target `column`), and places every task, superseding the hand-rolled create-project(1) + create-bucket(x3) + bulk-create(1) + bulk-set-bucket(x3-9) path this scenario used to measure. optimalCallCount: setup-kanban (1). A controlled haiku sweep (main @ 8c49b68) already measured actual=1 here, confirming the composite genuinely reaches this floor -- the stale optimal of 9 was letting the agent beat its own 'optimum', which made the friction ratio meaningless.
promptTemplate: Create a project called "{{prefix}}Sprint Board" with a kanban board with three columns: "{{prefix}}To Do", "{{prefix}}Doing", and "{{prefix}}Done". Add 9 tasks named "{{prefix}}task-1" through "{{prefix}}task-9". Then, in bulk (not one task at a time), distribute the tasks evenly across the three columns: "{{prefix}}task-1" through "{{prefix}}task-3" into "{{prefix}}To Do", "{{prefix}}task-4" through "{{prefix}}task-6" into "{{prefix}}Doing", and "{{prefix}}task-7" through "{{prefix}}task-9" into "{{prefix}}Done".
